text:
Faculty reviews: 
reviews are subjective, what worked for me might not necessarily work for you. Also, we sometimes don't get to do our preferred faculty's classes and that's okay, sometimes you're in your first semester and you walk to classes blindly and for me the faculty reviews helps me understand what the teacher might be like and what i might be expecting rather than being put off about not getting the 'best' faculty, again what might be considered best to you is not necessarily best for me. 
ENG103: ALR 
Miss takes 4, counts 3 quizzes, 5 essays and one multi-draft which she spends a lot of time in. She gave us 2 classes to complete the multi draft and she spent a lot of time on descriptive essays, she uses a lot of different mediums to teach like different texts from different books not just the coursebook, podcasts, and also interviews. The best thing about her classes were that she's always trying to help us improve doesn't matter how mediocre you write. Overall miss is very helpful and her classes are enjoyable but she does have some rules, honestly they are very basic rules every class has like be on time, don't use your phone and never use AI for writing. 
BIO103 - FHo 
She takes 4 quizzes and counts 3, takes a viva alongside midterm and final. Her slides are very precise and clear so it's not difficult to follow her, she is very lenient with marking, as long as you know the content you're good but i would suggest to write in an organized manner cuz miss prefers that. She is also very easy-going and is always there to help you out. She takes the viva on final exam topics and she gives exact suggestions so you don't have to really struggle there. Overall, she's one of the nicest teachers ever! 
BIO201: FZD 
Just no. Don't take his classes and not because he is going to give you a bad grade but also because he cannot teach. He came to class and read off slides, his slides are very VERY disorganised. The course itself is lengthy and has a lot of information since his slides are not organised, you have to organise them and also teach yourself the entire content throughout the semester. Some of the questions are directly and some are from God knows where. He gave us additional topics for our midterm in the class prior to our midterm so you have to study the new content on top of the old content a day before your midterm while midterms of other courses are also going on. If you do end up in his class, make sure you sit in the front, and enter his classes knowing that when you go home you're gonna have to teach yourself the entire content. :))
CHE202: MIO 
Being someone who is downright terrified of organic chemistry, sir's classes were one of the best decisions i made. I learnt a lot, and not just because i had to but learnt with interest too. He is really good at explaining stereochemistry and organic reactions which honestly, is what the entire course consists of. He made us practice a lot and gave many opportunities to achieve a good grade. He takes 4 quizzes from which he counts 2, he also gave us an assignment to improve our marks, although the assignment is a bit challenging, sir still gave a decent mark. Sir is very lenient with marking, he gave us bonus questions. He also does partial marking so even if you write something, he will give you partial marks. 
CHE203: Mkun 
Sir took 4 quizzes and counted 3. He also took a few assignments worth 5 marks alongside mid and final. He gave us plenty of time to prepare for the midterm and he is very lenient with marking. The only problem is he is a bit difficult to understand, he is likely to forget the chapters he excludes from the syllabus so make sure you learn everything, he doesn't give suggestions directly, if you follow his classes attentively you'll figure out which part is important. His final questions are very easy, while the mid is a tad bit challenging and very lengthy, still it's not that difficult to get a good mark. His slides are disorganised and the information are repetitive, apart from that be in his classes on time and do not be on your phone and you're good!  
BBT221: TSHq 
One of the best things i did in 2025 was to take her classes!! This was the one class i was always excited to do, i've learnt so much from her in 3.5 months, after a disastrous experience with FZD her classes reminded me why i chose to study biochem. The classes are definitely packed with heavy content but her slides and her teaching style is so organised that it didn't feel like so much work. Miss provided sample questions before every quiz, midterm and final. Although none of the questions were common it laid a good foundation before the exams. Her questions are slightly different but as long as you know the content, it's not that difficult. She focuses a lot on conceptual understanding rather than meaningless memorization and that really helps in understanding the content itself. Overall, even though it will require hardwork, it is 100% worth doing her classes, i came out of this class with so much more appreciation and understanding of what i study.  
HIS103: SAR3 
Sir is a storyteller, he will literally teach you the content as if he is telling you a story. he focuses a lot on understanding and some questions focuses on understanding of a specific event, he will not give direct suggestions but he will tell you which lecture is important and what kind of questions (broad/short) will be coming from each lecture. In spite of that, his slides are designed in such a way that he need not give suggestions, you will understand what kind of questions might come in both mid and final. He took 3 quizzes and counted 2. He also took an assignment worth 15 marks. The only one thing he doesn't do is provide feedback on the broad questions and where you went wrong but apart from that his classes are easy to grasp and enjoyable as well, he also screened movies for us to watch in class! 
POL101: RSU 
Another class that changed my perspective and helped me become more mindful. Sir is a foreign faculty and while he is a bit difficult to understand, it's not like there is a huge communication gap. Even if you don't understand something, his slides are more than enough to explain the content. They are well organised and to the point. His quizzes are pretty easy too and he literally provides sample questions before mid and final. He also takes a viva worth 10 marks and an assignment, before the assignment he provides sample and it's important that you don't use AI and make sure you choose topics from the POL101 coursebook. The presentation that he takes is very structured, make sure you run your draft through him before presenting. A great thing is that he literally provides detailed feedback on each group's presentation and for me, it helped in knowing where i went wrong and how i can improve. Overall, a great faculty and a very fun class! See less
